//12: TILES (looks_like): mon_shadow renders as a featureless black humanoid silhouette in UltimateCataclysm (data/json/monsters/nether.json:1308 is the base object; the sprite was checked directly).  That is as close as any existing sprite comes to the article's 'a face with no visible pupils, nostrils, or mouth' - a blank dark figure at human height.  Cosmetic only: looks_like is read exclusively by the tile drawer (src/cata_tiles.cpp, the mtype case at :2026), so it changes nothing about how it moves, fights or is spawned, and a tileset that ever draws mon_scp_087_1 itself wins automatically.
//: SCP-087-1.  From the article: 'a face with no visible pupils, nostrils, or mouth... not the source of the pleading.  Subjects exhibit feelings of intense paranoia and fear when faced with SCP-087-1.'  In the dark of the stairwell the player mostly sees the blank dark shape of it behind them - a barely-seen figure with a face that is nothing but skin.
description: A shape in the dark behind you, roughly human height, closer than it should be.  When the light catches it wrong you see a face with no pupils, no nostrils, no mouth - just flat skin where features should be.  It does not approach while you are moving away, and it does not go away.  It is not the thing that is crying.
//11: HP IS THE INVULNERABILITY (playtest fix).  The design is 'damage cannot reduce its HP or kill it, but each solid hit staggers it'.  That used to be attempted by an EOC that healed the monster on every hit - which never worked, and emitted `DEBUG : invalid body part id "ALL"` while not working.  The proof is in monster_attacks/scp_087_1_attacks.json //3b-3d; the short version is that no JSON primitive can write a monster's HP.  The write half of u_hp() is set_all_parts_hp_cur, which touches the creature's body-part map, and a monster's real HP is the single monster::hp field - monster overrides only the getters, and they ignore the bodypart argument (src/monster.cpp:4072-4089), so part writes never reach it.  What JSON CAN set is this field, because those same getters read type->hp.  So the number below is not a health pool: 100000 is 'this cannot be killed'.  No attack in the game comes close to it, which is the point - the pursuer's job is to be unoutrunable and unbeatable, and the player learns that by hitting it rather than by being told.  The stagger still fires on every solid hit, because monster_takes_damage is unaffected.  If upstream ever exposes a monster heal or damage immunity, this can drop back to a normal number with a working heal.
//2: TRANSFORMATION OMISSION (the README's hard-won rule, applied): zombify_into, fungalize_into, burn_into and revive_forms are all omitted, and upgrades is false.  It is an anomaly, not a corpse - it never rots, catches, or turns into a fungal version of itself.
//3: DEDICATED PLAYER-ONLY FACTION: it is assigned scp_087 (see monster_factions.json), which hates ONLY the player.  It ignores zombies, wildlife, NPCs and pets entirely - the face exists for you alone.
//5: ALWAYS_SEES_YOU - it can never be hidden from; the stalk is relentless.
//6: KEEP_DISTANCE + tracking_distance - it holds its distance behind the player and paces them (JSON_FLAGS.md:1214, enforced monster.cpp:1916-1917 and monmove.cpp:1145-1147).  This is the 'never outrun, never catch' trailing.  TWO NOTES (verified, B7/N2): the flag also makes the monster FLEE while it is INSIDE tracking_distance, so it backs off again after EOC_SCP_087_1_FOLLOW closes the gap - see the N2 note in scp_087_1_pursuer.json, that retreat is intended; and the code default for tracking_distance when the key is omitted is 8 with a floor of 3 (src/monstergenerator.cpp:904-905), NOT the 3 that doc/JSON/MONSTERS.md:135 documents.  We set 4 explicitly, so the behaviour here does not depend on which is right.
//7: STUN_IMMUNE - so staggers can't stunlock it into staying put.
//8: NEVER_WANDER - it stays out of wandering hordes and won't drift off to despawn (monster.cpp:4208).
//9: NOT_SET - CAN_OPEN_DOORS (it must not leave the shaft) and ALL_SEEING (it must not see through walls).
//10: NOT_HALLUCINATION - WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT DO (B7).  This flag is ONLY consulted when the engine builds the pool of monsters a RANDOM hallucination can become: MonsterGenerator::finalize adds every type without the flag to hallucination_monsters (src/monstergenerator.cpp:480-484), which get_valid_hallucination() draws from (:1265-1268).  It does NOT gate an explicitly named hallucination: the hallucination_count path used by EOC_SCP_087_PARANOIA resolves the named mtype and calls game::spawn_hallucination( p, mt, lifespan ) (src/npctalk.cpp:7703-7731 -> src/game.cpp:4709-4729), which never checks the flag.  So the hallucination beat works, and the flag's real job is to keep 087-1 out of OTHER sources of random hallucinations (cursed artifacts, portals, etc.) where a phantom of the anomaly would muddy the fiction.  Do not cite this flag as the reason the hallucination layer works - it is not.
